method: Flesch-Kincaid estimated age = 0.39 * words / sentence_units + 11.8 * syllables / words - 15.59 + 5. Each punctuated sentence or standalone line is a sentence unit. Same fixed vowel-group heuristic and overrides as the exemplar. These are text estimates, not learner assessments. Staff notes, running headers/footers and document locators are excluded. Pupil page headings, diagram labels, definitions and answer-reveal text are included. File-name stems are counted as alphabetic word groups.

rules: Lowercase; strip possessive apostrophe s and remaining apostrophes.
Subtract final silent e unless consonant-le ending, when count exceeds one.
Subtract final ed except ted or ded, when count exceeds one.

surfaces.text:
Spreadsheet formulas

surfaces.label: slide_2
surfaces.text:
Check the starting data
Watch the adult check one input.
A neat table can still have errors.
Compare one cell with the model data.
Model sheet
B4 = 2 packs
C4 = 3 points each
Show one matching value privately.

surfaces.label: slide_3
surfaces.text:
Find a cell
Columns have letters. Rows have numbers.
B4 is in column B, row 4.
Select C5 and find its value.
B4: column B, row 4
C5: column C, row 5
Point or click; you do not need to read aloud.
On the Model sheet C5 contains 2.

surfaces.label: slide_4
surfaces.text:
Build a row formula
Select D4 on the Model sheet.
Type =B4*C4, then press Enter.
The star * means multiply.
Select D4 again to see the formula.
B4 = 2     C4 = 3
D4: =B4*C4
Result: 6
Watch the formula and the result.

surfaces.label: slide_5
surfaces.text:
Total the rows
Complete D5 and D6 with their own rows.
Use =SUM(D4:D6) in D7.
D4:D6 means D4 through D6.
Change B4 to 4. Watch the totals.
Before: 6 + 6 + 4 = 16
B4 changes: 2 to 4
After: 12 + 6 + 4 = 22
Predict first, then check the update.

surfaces.label: slide_6
surfaces.text:
Formula signs
= starts the formula.
* means multiply.
D4:D6 is a range of three cells.
SUM adds the values in that range.
=B4*C4
=SUM(D4:D6)
Match a sign to its job in private.

surfaces.label: slide_7
surfaces.text:
A formula for the next row
Use the Task sheet from the workbook.
Check the six inputs against the data card.
Build D4, then try the next row.
Use the row number that matches the item.
Task: B4 = 3, C4 = 4
Task: B5 = 2, C5 = 5
Task: B6 = 4, C6 = 2
Show the formula, not just the answer.

surfaces.label: slide_8
surfaces.text:
Will the total update?
D4 contains the typed number 12.
B4 changes from 3 to 5.
Will that typed 12 update on its own?
Typed value: 12
Fixed formula: =3*4
Linked formula: =B4*C4
Choose yes or no privately, with a reason.
No. The typed 12 stays 12.
=B4*C4 follows changes in B4 and C4.

surfaces.label: slide_11

Complete D4, D5 and D6 with row formulas.

surfaces.label: slide_12
surfaces.text:
Aspire
Complete the Independent task first.
Predict D6 and D7 if B6 changes from 4 to 0. Test it.
Explain why 0 and an empty cell can mean different things.
Check that each row formula uses its own row.
Restore B6 to 4 and keep B4 at 5. Check the total.
Zero: no packs needed
Blank: check what is missing
Restore the task inputs.
Explain the meaning as well as the calculation.

surfaces.label: slide_13

surfaces.label: slide_14
surfaces.text:
A new input to test
An item uses 2 packs at 6 points each.
A formula gives 12 points.
The quantity changes to 3 packs.
What should the linked formula show now?
Before: 2 x 6 = 12
Change quantity: 2 to 3
After: 3 x 6 = ?
Give a private answer, then reopen your saved file.
18 points. The quantity changed from 2 to 3.

surfaces.label: pupil_page_2
surfaces.text:
Words for spreadsheets
cell
One box in a spreadsheet.
cell reference
The column letter and row number, such as B4.
input
A value you enter or change.
formula
An instruction that starts with = and works out a result.
range
A group of cells, such as D4:D6.
recalculate
Work out the results again when an input changes.
A useful reason
My formula uses ... so the result changes when ...

surfaces.label: pupil_page_3
surfaces.text:
Knowledge organiser
The aim
I can use cell references in formulas and check that totals update.
Cell references
B4 means column B, row 4. References link the formula to the input cells.
Formula signs
= starts a formula. * multiplies. SUM adds a range. D4:D6 means D4, D5 and D6.
Check carefully
Check the formula as well as the displayed answer. A typed result does not update. Check any blank input before trusting the total.
My success checks
[ ] I used cell references in my formulas.
[ ] I checked the row results and whole total.
[ ] I changed an input and checked the new total.
[ ] I saved and reopened my own workbook.
Where this leads
Office and stock roles use spreadsheets to check quantities. Explaining a formula gives evidence of a digital skill for an application.

Calculate
D4 = quantity x points each for row 4. Do the same for rows 5 and 6. D7 adds the three row totals.
Change test

Keep the right sheet
